The existing successful reference and retained BV/UFBV tactic caller fixtures pass in ordinary and `g3debug g3trace` builds on CPUs 8-16; focused vet and source-aware portcheck pass. The manifest credits this one `ref<goal>` path while `ref.h` and the whole util port remain partial.

Global-parameter debug memory-wrapper increment: retained `gparams::init` now emits the `memory::allocate(file,line,obj,size)` record immediately after its concrete Go owner-header reservation and before `imp` member construction; `gparams::finalize` emits the matching deallocation record after completed destruction. The generated process binds its actual memory finalization flag, suppressing that deallocation record during `mem_finalize` as in the source. Go pointer and charged Go header extent replace native address and `sizeof(imp)`. Checked trace fixtures cover exact record order, finalizing suppression and refused-stream continuation; full ordinary and `g3debug g3trace` params/process package suites and source-aware portcheck pass on CPUs 8-16. The manifest credits these concrete wrapper sites as platform replacements while other memory-manager call sites and the wider util port remain partial.

Global-parameter module-cell debug memory-wrapper increment: retained `gparams::imp::get_params` now emits the source `alloc(params_ref)` memory record when it creates a module cell, and `reset` and the destructor emit its matching deallocation record. A repeated lookup reuses the cell. Checked trace fixtures cover exact source-site records and release order before `imp`, process-finalizing suppression, and refused-stream continuation; full ordinary and checked params/process suites pass on CPUs 8-16. The manifest credits these concrete sites as platform replacements; other memory-manager callers and the wider util port remain partial.

Global-parameter late-binding correction: rebinding the namespace trace or process accounting flag after `gparams::init` now updates the live `imp` and any retained superseded or failed owners. Module-cell allocation follows the current trace stream, and module-cell deletion observes the current process-finalizing guard. A checked trace fixture binds both dependencies after initialization and verifies the allocation record moves to the new stream while finalization suppresses deallocation. The source `gparams` and memory-manager units remain partial.

Generated module-descriptor memory-wrapper increment: the 32 live `alloc(param_descrs)` sites in `src/shell/gparams_register_modules.cpp:40-71` now trace at the actual Go descriptor-header reservation. Duplicate-name merges emit the `gparams.cpp:143` deallocation after deleting the incoming descriptor, and `imp` destruction emits the `gparams.cpp:108` deallocation for the 19 retained module owners. A checked trace fixture verifies every allocation site, the 13 duplicate deletions, and the 19 destructor deletions; the finalizing and refused-stream fixtures also exercise catalog registration. Go pointers and charged header extents replace native addresses and `sizeof(param_descrs)`. Other memory-manager callers and the wider util port remain partial.

Generated symbol-table memory-wrapper increment: `initialize_symbols` now emits the `symbol.cpp:67` allocation record at the concrete Go manager reservation before member construction, and `finalize_symbols` emits the `symbol.cpp:72` deallocation after completed close. The generated process binds its trace owner and memory-finalizing flag before symbol initialization. Checked fixtures verify exact records, pointer-present reuse, null finalization, refused-stream continuation, generated symbol-before-gparams allocation order, and finalizing suppression; Go pointer and charged header extent replace the native address and `sizeof(internal_symbol_table)`. The symbol source unit remains ported, while other memory-manager wrapper callers and the wider util port remain partial.

Generated rational-manager memory-wrapper increment: `rational::initialize` now emits the `rational.cpp:66` `alloc(synch_mpq_manager)` record at the concrete Go manager-header reservation before its integer child construction. Successful `rational::finalize` emits the `rational.cpp:82` deallocation record after the manager's source destructor; separate Go owning close still refunds the retained header. The generated process binds its trace before rational initialization. Checked fixtures verify exact records, pointer-present reuse, refused-stream continuation, finalizing suppression and rational-before-symbol-before-gparams allocation order. Other rational global lifecycle gaps and memory-manager callers keep their source units partial.

Parameter-descriptor inner memory-wrapper increment: `param_descrs` construction now emits its `params.cpp:211` `alloc(imp)` record before dictionary member construction, and completed destruction emits the `params.cpp:215` deallocation record. The stable Go descriptor-entry field identifies the inner state separately from the outer descriptor, and the combined charged Go descriptor header replaces native `sizeof(imp)`. Checked fixtures verify the embedded global descriptor's order inside `gparams::imp`, 34 catalog inner allocations, 15 early inner deletions, 20 final inner deletions, late trace rebinding, finalizing suppression and refused-stream continuation. Other `params.cpp` allocation sites and the wider util port remain partial.

Parameter-block memory-wrapper increment: first `params_ref::init` and shared copy-on-write now emit `alloc(params)` records at `params.cpp:600/605`; the final `params::dec_ref` destructor emits the `params.cpp:339` deallocation record after entry cleanup. Native Go blocks occupy a growable typed directory, so records use the stable context-owner/slot/generation identity and charged Go block extent rather than a moving slice address. A checked fixture forces directory relocation and verifies first/COW records pair with their final releases; generated-process finalizing and refused-stream fixtures exercise real block lifetimes. Other parameter ownership paths and the wider util port remain partial.

Parameter rational-entry memory-wrapper increment: the live `SET_RAT_VALUE` new-entry and matched-scalar branches now emit `alloc(rational)` at `params.cpp:1004/996`, and completed `del_value` paths emit the `params.cpp:757` deallocation. Each inline Go `OwnedRational` carries a stable context-owner/setter-invocation trace identity through page growth and suffix shifts. Checked fixtures verify matched-rational reuse adds no allocation and that replacement, key reset, live reset and last-reference cleanup each release the correct identity; generated finalization suppresses deallocation records, while refused trace output leaves ownership cleanup intact. Other parameter ownership gaps and the wider util port remain partial.

Trace tag-table memory-wrapper increment: the first `enable_trace` or `disable_trace` table creation emits the `trace.cpp:31` allocation record when `enable_all_trace(true)` was already active. Enabling `memory` in a newly created table cannot retroactively trace that allocation. Finalization emits the `trace.cpp:37` deallocation record when the source all flag keeps tracing defined after the table is destroyed, and the generated process's finalizing guard suppresses it. The Go map header supplies the native allocation-size field and its owner's tag field supplies a stable identity. Other trace call sites and the wider util port remain partial.

Debug tag-table memory-wrapper increment: lazy `enable_debug`, `disable_debug`, or `is_debug_enabled` initialization now emits the `debug.cpp:48` allocation record, and `finalize_debug` emits the `debug.cpp:53` deallocation record. Both use the generated process's selected trace owner; finalizing suppresses deallocation records, and owning close restores the prior trace binding. Checked fixtures cover lazy reconstruction, null finalization and the process finalization guard. Other debug.cpp behavior and the wider util port remain partial.

Top-level unported-header consumer audit: `list.h`, `obj_pair_set.h`, `plugin_manager.h`, `pool.h` and `scoped_vector.h` have production specializations in unported SMT owners (`smt_types`, conflict resolution, proto-model, MAM and theory sequence). The test-only list use does not justify a generic Go port. Their concrete typed storage belongs in those owners when those owners are ported. The recent debug/trace table allocation sites are now credited in both `memory_manager.cpp` and `memory_manager.h`; their remaining wrapper sites still need consumer-by-consumer audit.

Raw word-access performance increment: `Runtime.ReadUint32` and `WriteUint32` now validate the live block, source size header and whole-word bounds once per word, then inspect or publish the same four initialized bytes in order. This removes repeated block/header lookups from every MPZ limb access without changing the source numerical algorithms, allocation counts or byte initialization semantics; a crossing-bitmap-boundary fixture covers the less common case. Ordinary and checked memory tests, the full numeral suite, the independent exact-LU oracle and the previously reported LP diagnostic tests pass. A broad `go test ./util/...` attempt hit Go's default ten-minute timeout after cumulative LP tests; its independent oracle passes in about five seconds, so the broad timeout is not evidence of that oracle hanging. A subsequent `go test ./util/lp -count=1 -timeout 10m` on CPUs 8-16 also timed out, during `TestLPExactLeavingPhysicalOwnership/ratio/true/163`. That test sweeps up to 1,600 allocation-failure positions for each of eight cases; the timeout did not report an assertion failure and does not establish a full-package pass. The wider util port remains partial.

LP physical-ownership verification increment: `TestLPExactLeavingPhysicalOwnership` now nests its eight independent operation/storage cases above their allocation-failure ordinals. This preserves every checked failure position and lets a single case be selected with `go test -run` after the cumulative package timeout. The complete ownership test passes in ordinary and combined `g3debug g3trace` builds on CPUs 8-16; the entire LP package has not yet passed within Go's default ten-minute timeout.

Shell scoped-timer memory-wrapper increment: the live `set_timeout` path now observes `scoped_timer.cpp:257/264` allocation and deallocation of its concrete `imp` counterpart. Disabled intervals skip the record; replacement releases the old timer before allocating the next, and the bound process-finalizing flag suppresses the deletion record. The Go timer owner pointer and header extent replace the native address and `sizeof(imp)`. Focused ordinary and combined `g3debug g3trace` shell/control suites and source-aware portcheck pass on CPUs 8-16. Other memory-wrapper callers and the wider util port remain partial.

Scoped-timer process guard correction: the shell timer trace now reads finalization from its borrowed `TraceTags`, which the generated process already binds to the shared memory owner. A standalone shell owner can borrow that same trace without a second process binding. Ordinary and checked diagnostic, control, shell and portcheck suites pass on CPUs 8-16.

Utility CPU-timer memory-wrapper increment: `timer::timer` now emits its `timer.cpp:25` `alloc(stopwatch)` record before the actual Go watch starts; `Close` emits the matching `timer.cpp:30` deallocation once, including after a retained constructor clock failure. The borrowed process trace suppresses deallocation during generated finalization. The inline Go watch address and extent replace the native pointer and `sizeof(stopwatch)`. Focused ordinary and combined `g3debug g3trace` stopwatch tests plus source-aware portcheck pass on CPUs 8-16. The SMT timer consumer and other memory-wrapper sites remain open.

Utility timeit memory-wrapper increment: enabled `timeit` construction now emits `timeit.cpp:50` `alloc(imp)` before its first memory or clock read; disabled scopes emit nothing. Completed reports emit `timeit.cpp:57` deallocation after their final output, while a failed Go construction or report retains its owner until explicit `Cleanup`. The shared trace's process-finalizing guard suppresses deallocation output. Inline Go owner identity and extent replace the native imp pointer and size. Focused ordinary and combined `g3debug g3trace` stopwatch tests pass on CPUs 8-16; SMT and Spacer production report callers remain unported.

MPF powers-cache memory-wrapper increment: each cold `powers2` cache miss now emits its actual `mpf.h:268` or `:282` `alloc(mpz)` record before publishing the new Go wrapper and numeral payload. Cache hits emit no allocation. Completed source or explicit owning cleanup emits the matching `mpf.h:258` deallocation once; generated process finalization suppresses the record. Go wrapper identity/header extent replace the native mpz pointer and size. Focused ordinary failure-prefix/cache tests, checked memory-trace tests and source-aware portcheck pass on CPUs 8-16. Remaining wrapper sites and the wider util port remain partial.

LP package verification: a single `go test ./util/lp -count=1 -timeout 30m` run completed successfully in 818.937 seconds on CPUs 8-16, confirming that the previous ten-minute timeouts were cumulative test duration rather than an LP assertion failure. Timer, timeit and MPF trace dependencies were edited while that long-running test binary was already executing; the current worktree was subsequently rebuilt and the previously reported LP diagnostic groups plus the exact-leaving ownership sweep passed in focused ordinary and combined `g3debug g3trace` runs. The long LP run is evidence for its launch revision, while current dependency changes have focused verification.

AIG tactic parameter-descriptor increment: the live `collect_param_descrs` method now registers `max_memory` through util/params and then `aig_per_assertion` with its source bool kind and description. Repeated collection preserves first insertion order; `aig_default_gate_encoding` remains absent, as in the source. Focused ordinary and combined `g3debug g3trace` tests pass on CPUs 8-16. Translation, generated registration, display, checked well-sorted assertions and the wider util port remain partial.

AIG tactic assertion increment: the retained goal-rewrite path now calls the concrete goal well-sorted checker at both `SASSERT` positions, after tactic-report construction and after rewriting, through the process debug switch. A malformed quantifier fixture verifies that the entry assertion refuses before manager construction and leaves the goal unchanged; successful AIG package tests exercise the post-rewrite check. Ordinary and combined `g3debug g3trace` AIG tests pass on CPUs 8-16. Bound assertion-action continuation and the wider util port remain partial.

AIG expression-cache destruction and TRACE increment: the retained `expr2aig` converter now closes cached AIG references before its result stack, matching the C++ destructor order. The `expr2aig` trace records each cached literal and its live reference count before decrement; a source variable fixture checks the exact gated record and count. Ordinary and combined `g3debug g3trace` AIG tests pass on CPUs 8-16. AST pretty-print-dependent AIG trace sites and the wider util port remain partial.

Optimized AIG-to-goal TRACE increment: source `aig2expr` records now follow auxiliary AND skips and successful AND or ITE/IFF cache publication, using the same concrete node IDs as deletion and expression-cache traces. A negative nested-AND fixture checks skip-before-cache order and an ITE fixture checks the separate cache record; ordinary and combined `g3debug g3trace` tests pass on CPUs 8-16. Remaining AIG trace sites and the wider util port remain partial.

AIG constructor memory-wrapper failure increment: the tactic's outer `alloc(aig_manager)` record now follows its successful owner reservation before the inner `alloc(imp)` attempt; the inner record follows its own successful reservation before true-node construction. Three injected constructor prefixes check no record before the outer reserve, only the outer record when the inner reserve fails, and both records when subsequent child construction fails. Go refunds failed owner reservations while source allocation TRACE retains the successful prefix without destructor records. Focused ordinary and combined `g3debug g3trace` AIG checks pass on CPUs 8-16. Other memory-wrapper callers and the wider util port remain partial.

AIG max-sharing traversal TRACE increment: the postorder loop now preserves C++ switch fallthrough when a child visit needs no frame, avoiding extra iteration records. The retained `processing` record prints the actual node and frame index before each source switch, and `r.is_null()` prints the pre-cache-reset result state. A nested-AND fixture checks entry, child-return and unchanged/improved result records in ordinary and combined `g3debug g3trace` builds on CPUs 8-16. The source display-dependent sharing records and the wider util port remain partial.

AIG max-sharing reassociation TRACE increment: all four retained `trying` records now print their source parenthesization and node references at the left/right candidate boundaries. The right branch's second record follows candidate construction, as in C++; a two-nested-child fixture checks all four exact headers, bodies and order in ordinary and combined `g3debug g3trace` builds on CPUs 8-16. Source `improved` and final-result records still need AIG display and AST expression printing; the wider util port remains partial.

AIG optimized-converter conditional TRACE increment: an uncached AND node now emits the retained `aig2expr` `invalid get_cached` record before the source assertion/lookup boundary; a populated cache suppresses the conditional record. A concrete AIG pair fixture checks the exact enabled record, erased build, and unchanged cache-error result in ordinary and combined `g3debug g3trace` builds on CPUs 8-16. AST SMT2 pretty-printing and the display-dependent AIG trace sites remain open, as does the wider util port.

AST SMT2 function-name prerequisite: `smt2_pp_environment::pp_fdecl_name` now constructs actual format-string nodes for quoted, numerical, null and simple symbols, and selects source `=>`, `ite` and `=` spellings for basic implication, ITE and IFF declarations before falling back to the declaration name. Focused ordinary and combined `g3debug g3trace` AST tests pass on CPUs 8-16. This begins the retained SMT2 printer path reached by AIG display and trace callers; expression traversal, layout, aliasing and the wider util port remain open.

AST SMT2 declaration-classification prerequisite: `is_indexed_fdecl` now walks actual declaration parameters in source order, accepts integer/rational/function-declaration references, and rejects null-family, empty and unsupported parameter lists. `is_sort_param` accepts only a sole sort parameter identical to the declaration range. Focused ordinary and combined `g3debug g3trace` AST tests cover these branches on CPUs 8-16. This advances the retained SMT2 printer needed by util TRACE callers; declaration format assembly, expression traversal and the wider util port remain open.

Concrete format-pointer sequence prerequisite: `format.h` `mk_seq1` now builds actual grouped format nodes for a header and ordered children, with source indentation, empty-list shape and nil-tail filtering. The helper queries the dedicated format manager when examining child kinds. Focused ordinary and combined `g3debug g3trace` tests check wide and narrow rendered documents on CPUs 8-16. This enables SMT2 indexed declaration and sort format assembly for retained util TRACE displays; those callers and the wider util port remain open.

AST SMT2 base sort formatter: `smt2_pp_environment::pp_sort` now constructs actual format nodes for Bool, Int, Real, indexed BitVec and FloatingPoint, recursive Array/Seq/RegEx, parametric datatype and plain named sorts. The existing AST sort metadata determines the source family and kind; `FormatSeq1` supplies grouped SMT2 layout. Focused ordinary and combined `g3debug g3trace` tests render each branch on CPUs 8-16. The command-context override for parametric sorts, declaration/expression assembly and retained util TRACE display callers remain open, as does the wider util port.

AST SMT2 declaration assembly: the base environment now constructs source `as` and indexed declaration formats, preserves the `UINT_MAX` compound-length sentinel, and prints recursive declaration references with nested `mk_seq5` domain/range signatures. Indexed parameter rendering consumes concrete integer, rational and function-declaration metadata, and the format owner now has the concrete `mk_seq5` grouping used by signatures. Focused ordinary and combined `g3debug g3trace` tests render plain, indexed, sort-qualified, nested and narrow signatures on CPUs 8-16. Expression traversal, aliasing, command-context sort overrides and the retained util TRACE displays remain open; the wider util port is incomplete.

LP remote-failure recheck and SMT2 variable/label formatting: the eight previously reported LP test groups now pass in both ordinary and combined `g3debug g3trace` builds on CPUs 8-16. The retained SMT2 printer's bound-variable reverse name lookup, quoted names, unbound `(:var i)` fallback, integer/symbol attributes and ordered positive/negative label format construction are ported and rendered by focused tests in both profiles. Frame info-stack integration, expression traversal, AIG display-dependent util TRACE records and the wider util port remain open.

SMT2 nonconstant application format branch: after child documents are available, `process_app` now constructs the source grouped short-name form with indentation `len+2` and the compound/long-name form with indentation 2. The concrete `mk_seq` tail preserves line breaks and skips nil suffix documents. Focused ordinary and combined `g3debug g3trace` tests render wide and narrow forms on CPUs 8-16. Child traversal, aliases, frame information and the AIG display-dependent util TRACE records remain open; the wider util port remains incomplete.

SMT2 selected Boolean tree traversal: a concrete child-before-parent walk now connects variable fallback, constant declaration names, nested Boolean applications and source positive/negative label formatting to the actual format owner. It rejects shared, flat-associative and deep-alias profiles until their source frame behavior is ported, and refuses numeric/quantifier cases rather than printing an incorrect fallback. Focused ordinary and combined `g3debug g3trace` tests render small source-equivalent Boolean atoms on CPUs 8-16. The retained AIG display-dependent util TRACE records still need a complete expression printer and stream integration; the wider util port remains open.

SMT2 function-declaration printer entrypoint: `smt2_printer::operator()(func_decl*,format_ref&)` now builds the source `declare-fun` document using the declaration's plain name, grouped domain sequence and printed range. Zero-arity, mixed Bool/BitVec and indexed-metadata declarations render exactly; the indexed case confirms this entrypoint uses `pp_fdecl_name`, not indexed `pp_fdecl`. Focused ordinary and combined `g3debug g3trace` tests pass on CPUs 8-16. AIG display still needs the full expression/stream path and the wider util port remains incomplete.

AST memory-wrapper process guard correction: format-manager, builtin, registered, arithmetic-plugin, parameter-rational and node-info deallocation records now query the owning AST numeral runtime's process as well as the borrowed trace's bound process. A checked fixture constructs a standalone AST manager with an unbound memory trace, enters its numeral runtime's process-finalization interval, and verifies allocation records remain visible while manager deallocation records are suppressed. Focused checked AST memory tests and source-aware portcheck pass on CPUs 8-16. Trace-file and sort-dependency owners still rely on their bound trace process; the wider util port remains incomplete.

AST file and sort-dependency memory-wrapper guard correction: the concrete trace-file owner now retains its AST manager even on a failed file construction, and the lexical sort-dependency owner borrows its manager before allocating its first set. Both deallocation records consult that manager's actual numeral process during finalization, including when the borrowed trace is unbound. The checked fixture now opens a real trace file and collects a real sort while finalizing, confirming both records are suppressed; ordinary AST source tests, checked memory tests and source-aware portcheck pass on CPUs 8-16. The broader util port remains incomplete.

MPF powers-cache memory-wrapper guard correction: `mpf.h:258` deallocation now consults the concrete arbitrary-float manager's runtime process as well as any process bound to its trace stream. The checked wrapper failure-prefix fixture deliberately leaves the trace unbound, enters the runtime's finalization interval and verifies the allocated wrapper is released without a deallocation record. Focused ordinary and checked MPF cache tests and source-aware portcheck pass on CPUs 8-16. Other retained util paths remain incomplete.

Model consumer memory-wrapper guard correction: retained model-copy, universe and copied-function deallocation records now query their owning AST numeral process in addition to any process bound to their trace; evaluator imp records query the validated evaluator runtime process. The universe header retains its AST manager for this lifetime check. Checked fixtures exercise real model/universe copy and function-copy lifetimes with an unbound trace during process finalization, while existing evaluator and normal memory-record tests retain their source text and order. Focused ordinary and checked model tests and source-aware portcheck pass on CPUs 8-16. The wider util memory-manager audit remains partial.

AIG consumer memory-wrapper guard correction: both the outer `aig_manager` and inner `imp` deallocation records now consult their AST manager's numeral runtime process as well as the borrowed trace. A checked fixture constructs the real two-part owner with an unbound trace, enters process finalization and verifies that both allocations remain visible while both deallocations are suppressed. Existing source-order and constructor-failure prefix checks, ordinary AIG checks and source-aware portcheck pass on CPUs 8-16. The broader util memory-manager audit remains partial.

Debug source-method audit: `notify_assertion_violation`, the selected classic-byte `std::cin >> char` prerequisite, and the Linux/NO_Z3_DEBUGGER `invoke_gdb` action are now credited as ported methods in both `debug.cpp` and `debug.h`. Existing concrete implementations preserve the four stderr insertion chains, borrowed C-string lifetime, tied-output input sentry, prompt/switch order, real exit and default-exception transport, and Linux command/signal action. Focused ordinary and combined `g3debug g3trace` diagnostic tests pass on CPUs 8-16. Global macro and retained caller audits still keep the source units partial.

SMT2 default flat-associative traversal increment: the selected Boolean expression printer now follows `smt2_printer::flat_assoc` for a nonshared child with the same associative declaration, leaving its ordered child documents for the parent and omitting the nested application document. A nested `and` renders as one source-default application; a repeated shared child still refuses until alias handling is ported. Focused ordinary and combined `g3debug g3trace` AST tests pass on CPUs 8-16. Numeric, quantifier and alias traversal plus retained util TRACE callers remain open.

SMT2 atomic occurrence increment: the selected Boolean-tree traversal now follows source `shared_occs` default `track_atomic=false`, printing repeated variables and zero-argument applications directly even when the same AST node occurs more than once. Repeated compound applications still refuse until source alias registration and let formatting are ported. Focused ordinary and combined `g3debug g3trace` fixtures cover repeated leaves inside flattened `and` and repeated bound variables on CPUs 8-16. This advances the retained AIG `expr2aig` TRACE printer prerequisite; stream integration and wider util TRACE remain open.

SMT2 shared-compound occurrence increment: a source-order prepass now counts incoming edges to each nonconstant application once per distinct parent graph, matching `shared_occs` default traversal. Selected Boolean formatting measures child weight and depth after flattening, suppresses `flat_assoc` for a shared child, and prints a repeated small compound directly when the default alias thresholds (weight 10, depth 5) do not apply. A shared two-child `and` renders twice inside its parent; a shared nine-argument `and` refuses until alias registration and `let` formatting are implemented. Focused ordinary and combined `g3debug g3trace` AST tests pass on CPUs 8-16. The AIG display stream and broader util TRACE paths remain open.

SMT2 let-layout increment: the source `pp_let` format construction now has a concrete Go helper that groups alias definitions by dependency level, emits each level's `(let ...)` binder in source order, and indents the body as the C++ formatter does. Focused ordinary and combined `g3debug g3trace` fixtures cover no bindings, one binding, same-level bindings and nested levels on CPUs 8-16. Alias registration and its integration with selected Boolean-tree traversal remain open; `src/ast/ast_smt2_pp.cpp` and the retained util TRACE path remain partial.

SMT2 selected Boolean alias increment: the retained expression traversal now registers source-default aliases when a nonroot compound reaches depth five or a shared compound reaches weight ten, reuses each alias on later visits, tracks alias dependency levels, and wraps the root in source `let` documents. Flat associative children still expose their argument documents and skip alias registration. Focused fixtures cover a shared large `and`, an alias-dependent shared `or`, a reserved alias name, and a depth-five implication chain, in ordinary and checked TRACE builds on CPUs 8-16. Numeric, quantified and wider retained TRACE printer paths remain open; the util port is still incomplete.

SMT2 arithmetic-child increment: the selected Boolean expression traversal now admits reached non-Boolean children and formats arithmetic numeral leaves using source-default exact integer and rational notation, including negative wrappers and real `.0` numerator/denominator forms. Non-Boolean family constants with unported literal rules still refuse rather than silently using declaration syntax. An actual Boolean equality over each numeral type checks the rendered format; the earlier eight reported LP failures also pass on the current tree. Decimal, irrational, BV, string, quantified and AIG stream-integration paths remain open, along with the util port.

SMT2 bit-vector-child increment: the same selected Boolean traversal now dispatches bit-vector numeral leaves to the already ported source literal formatter with default `bv_literals=true` and `bv_neg=false`. Concrete equality formulas verify hexadecimal, binary and negative-normalized numeral output at widths 4, 5 and 8; ordinary and checked TRACE focused tests pass on CPUs 8-16. String, floating-point, quantified and AIG stream-integration paths remain open, as does the util port.

SMT2 floating-point-child increment and special-value correction: the selected Boolean traversal now recognizes concrete FPA numerals and uses the source-default bit-vector-field printer. A live equality fixture exposed that `ppFloatLiteral` chose finite fields before checking source NaN/infinity/zero classes; the port now makes the source class checks first. Finite, positive-zero and NaN equality documents render with the correct source spelling. Focused ordinary and checked TRACE tests pass on CPUs 8-16; string, quantified and AIG stream-integration paths remain open, as does the util port.

Retained AIG cache TRACE integration: `expr2aig::cache_result` now emits its source record before the cache's owning reference acquisition, using the actual selected SMT2 Boolean format and the bound process parameter service to render both a variable and a shared compound. The existing destructor dec-ref record still follows cache release in source order. A checked-build fixture verifies the exact variable record and the compound body; ordinary and checked AIG package suites pass on CPUs 8-16. Non-Boolean, quantified and string expression profiles and other AIG display/TRACE sites remain open; util TRACE and the overall port stay partial.

Retained AIG display and max-sharing TRACE increment: the Go AIG owner now exposes the source breadth-first display of an inverted or normal root, gate children and variable SMT2 expressions, visiting shared children once with a local native map. `max_sharing` emits the source improved old/new displays after successful reassociation, then its final result display after pass-cache cleanup; the previously reached null-result record still precedes cleanup. Focused fixtures check exact simple display, shared-child visitation, and improved/result headers and root references; ordinary and checked AIG package suites pass on CPUs 8-16. Wider SMT2 variable profiles and other AIG display users remain open; util TRACE and the overall port remain partial.

Retained AIG AND TRACE increment: every source `imp::mk_and` route in the Go AIG owner now emits `mk_and_bug` after minimization, with the original left/right graph displays followed by the result display. This includes max-sharing's direct AND calls as well as public and goal-conversion calls; `InternAnd` still maps directly to the source `mk_node_core` path. A trace-format failure releases a newly interned unowned gate and its child references. AIG source-consumer audit: the source tree has only the declaration and two implementations of `aig_manager::display_smt2`/`imp::display_smt2`, with no call site; both are now recorded as reference-only under the retained-consumer rule. All reached AIG TRACE sites are represented in the `util/trace` inventory, including the newly ported `mk_and_bug` route. MPN single-limb decimal formatting increment: `sourceToCStringScopedTracked` now uses Go's `strconv.FormatUint` for the retained `mpn.cpp` one-limb decimal branch, while preserving the source's bounded destination writes, zero-size behavior and trace timing. The focused trace fixture also covers the maximum `uint32` value and its full ten-digit destination. Ordinary and checked/debug/trace focused numeral tests pass on CPUs 8–16. The multi-limb branch retains project division arithmetic, and the wider numeral lifetime port remains partial. The reported `pkg/util/log` is absent in this checkout; diagnostic tests pass in ordinary, checked, debug, trace and combined configurations, with 20 consecutive combined runs.

SMT2 local symbol-table reset audit: `smt2LocalEnv.reset` already discards the binding map, undo trail and open scope limits, matching `symbol_table<local>::reset` at the parser's `smt2parser.cpp:3003` call. The reset method row is now marked ported. The wider parser and the remaining concrete `symbol_table.h` call sites remain partial.

MPFX floor/ceil overflow correction: source `mpfx_manager::floor/ceil` zeroes fractional words before incrementing the fixed-width integer part, and `bit_util::inc` wraps every integer word to zero before returning overflow. The concrete Go numeric value now becomes zero on that reached carry overflow instead of retaining its pre-call value. Focused ordinary and checked/debug/trace tests cover positive ceil and negative floor overflow, plus normal rounding and trace output, on CPUs 8–16. The source's retained allocated word slot and negative zero sign after a thrown overflow are not represented by `big.Int`; those exceptional ownership/sign details and the wider MPFX port remain partial.

MPFX exceptional zero-word state increment: `FixedPoint` now retains the source allocated-slot marker and prior sign after floor/ceil carry overflow alongside its zero `big.Int` words. `is_zero` distinguishes that state from canonical zero; positive/negative predicates and ordering, copy, swap, reset, sign changes, display, and the source power-zero branch use the retained marker. A focused fixture exercises both sign variants and transitions after a throw. Full ordinary and checked/debug/trace numeral package tests and focused portcheck checks pass on CPUs 8–16. Physical pool ownership, assertion behavior on the inconsistent post-throw source state and its other arithmetic remain partial.

MPFX nonexceptional zero-word state increment: the retained `mul` nonzero-operand branch and noninteger `mpq` setter can publish zero quotient words without calling `reset`, leaving an allocated source slot and a sign bit. The concrete Go paths now preserve that marker after successful underflow, including aliased multiplication and the rational setter's prior-destination sign rule. Canonical-zero operands still take the source reset branch. Focused ordinary and checked/debug/trace `TestFixedPoint` campaigns pass on CPUs 8–16. Source debug assertions on allocated zero words, physical pool ownership and other exceptional arithmetic remain partial.

MPFX zero-word add/sub increment: `add_sub` distinguishes canonical zero from an allocated zero-word slot. The concrete Go path now preserves the slot when a canonical-zero shortcut copies or negates one, retains same-sign zero-word sums, and resets opposite-sign cancellation. The inner `mpfx` trace now runs for two allocated zero-word operands as in the source. Focused ordinary and checked/debug/trace `TestFixedPoint` campaigns pass on CPUs 8–16. Division's quotient-zero branch already resets or emits an epsilon according to directed rounding; broader source assertion and pool lifetime details remain partial.

MPFX add/sub carry-overflow correction: fixed-width `bit_util::add` writes each destination word before returning a carry, and `mpfx_manager::add_sub` throws after those writes. Concrete Go Add/Sub and the retained Inc/Dec routes now publish the low wrapped words and source sign before returning `ErrFixedPointOverflow`, including an allocated zero-word slot when the wrapped magnitude is zero. Focused fixtures cover positive/negative wraps, aliased outputs, zero-slot classification, and the missing post-overflow result trace; ordinary and checked/debug/trace `TestFixedPoint` campaigns pass on CPUs 8–16. The wider source word-pool and assertion behavior remains partial.

MPFX multiplication-overflow publication correction: source `mpfx_manager::mul` calls `allocate_if_needed(c)` and sets `c.m_sign` before multiplication/rounding overflow checks, but copies product words only after both checks succeed. The concrete Go path now preserves old destination magnitude and publishes the new sign before returning overflow; a canonical-zero destination acquires the source allocated-slot marker. Focused ordinary and checked/debug/trace tests cover distinct nonzero and zero destinations, both signs, aliased output and the absent result trace on CPUs 8–16. Physical pool allocation/failure timing and source assertions remain partial.

MPFX division-overflow publication correction: after the denominator-zero guard, source `mpfx_manager::div` allocates the destination slot and assigns the quotient sign before computing/checking the temporary quotient. On quotient or rounding overflow it throws before copying words. The concrete Go path now shares the multiplication failure-state publication: old destination words remain, the new sign is visible, and a formerly canonical zero retains a slot. Focused ordinary and checked/debug/trace tests cover both signs, nonzero/zero destinations, aliased output and the absent result trace on CPUs 8–16. Physical pool failure timing and source assertions remain partial.

MPFX numeral-conversion overflow prefix: source `set_core(mpz)` allocates the destination slot and assigns the incoming sign before checking decomposed integer-word count; its noninteger `set_core(mpq)` allocates a slot and preserves the old sign before checking total-word count. The concrete Go conversion paths now retain old destination words and publish those reached slot/sign prefixes on overflow, including an acquired negative or positive zero-word slot. The integer-valued rational branch follows the integer setter. Focused ordinary and checked/debug/trace `TestFixedPoint` campaigns pass on CPUs 8–16. Physical pool allocation and assertion timing remain partial.

MPN raw-display insertion correction: `display_raw`'s opening bracket, each descending decimal limb, separators and closing bracket now use the same Go short-write check as the other concrete numeral display paths. MPN unnormalized-denominator source assertion: the internal division engine now checks the source `SASSERT(denom[lden-1] != 0)` at `mpn.cpp:179` after the all-zero scan. MPN post-division verification assertion: after the `mpn_dbg` conditional TRACE at `mpn.cpp:215`, a false checked verification now reaches the process-bound source `SASSERT(ok)` action at line 216. Parameter matched-rational allocation-frontier audit: source `SET_RAT_VALUE` at `params.cpp:992-1000` publishes `CPK_NUMERAL` after deleting an old nonnumeral entry and before `alloc(rational)`. The concrete Go `setMatchedNewNumeral` publishes the numeral entry after `RationalService.NewValue`; this service call allocates no storage and only checks its owner lock. `ParamsContext.set` already validates the same service via `IsRational` before initialization and key lookup, and no intervening operation on the matched nonnumeral path can close or mutate that borrowed service in the current single-goroutine port. Thus there is no reachable stopped Go operation between the source kind write and the existing Go publication. The later rational Copy remains a real failure boundary: `setMatchedNewNumeral` publishes the numeral entry and its exact copy receipt before Copy, and existing postphysical tests verify stopped owning cleanup. No synthetic allocation/error adapter was added. The broader params_ref clone/reset/refcount paths remain partial.

size again for composite hashing. Raw-prefix query tests leave refcount unreadable
in both branches; zero also leaves flags unreadable. The nonzero fixture runs
actual lexical sorting and matches the hash of the genuine owning polynomial.

mk_unique inserted its bucket only after the owning reference-vector push;

unreadable, so the actual guarded INC read stops after table publication. The
entry remains present without an acquired reference or cached ID; retry hits
that table entry without attempting INC again. This is guarded access-order
evidence, not an ordinary C++ INC allocation failure. Every query restores the
genuine owning record before destruction; no source-construction flags or fake
ownership metadata are introduced.

Datatype model-based projection prerequisite (2026-10-24): ported the retained datatype_project_plugin from qe_datatypes.cpp/.h as concrete DatatypeProjection. Projection evaluates the target, preserves the absent/nonconstructor-model-value early return and selects recursive or nonrecursive constructor handling using the existing datatype utilities. Recursive solving finds the first usable equality, follows constructor accessors toward the target, and emits sibling field equalities and recognizers in source unwind order. No synthetic cant_project adapter is introduced because the retained implementation has no throwing path for that exception.

The datatype cheap-solve hook lifts non-Boolean, non-datatype projection variables from constructor equalities. Its memoized app-only traversal, right-constructor preference, raw recognizer/field equalities and swap-with-last residue order preserve source choices. Retained asserted-formula driver control flow (2026-10-24): replaced the kernel's unconditional preprocessing sequence with concrete retained pass dispatch in smt_asserted_driver.go. The driver follows asserted_formulas::reduce order, including the preliminary stored-macro invocation, pre/post-NNF conjunction phase, repeated macro discovery and final ordinary rewrite/cache reset. Source should_apply policy controls invocation; skipped passes do not poll cancellation or increment its resource count. Active passes stop the driver on inconsistency or cancellation. A canceled driver leaves the commit cursor pending for reuse; an inconsistent result still reaches the internalizer to establish UNSAT.

Assertions now preserve the source sticky has-quantifiers flag from the original input, even when rewriting removes the quantifier; scope pop leaves it set. Quantifier-sensitive macro, NNF, pattern, distribution, pulling, bound and injectivity guards use that manager state. New assertions after an existing false formula are ignored before preprocessing, and recursive assertion flattening stops accepting children after false. Value propagation now performs the source single forward/reverse pair (++num_iterations < 2), followed by ordinary reduction when changed. Macro/NNF post-operations no longer run extra value-propagation rounds. Previously removed macro definitions still expand when discovery/preprocessing options are later disabled, retaining the documented native repair.

The older term-ITE guard test now explicitly enters the source driver's post-NNF phase before requiring three flattened rows; a separate regression verifies the pre-phase unchanged-conjunction behavior.

Raw vector swapping now performs no rewriting, flattening or extra cancellation polling. Macro discovery/quasi-macro/native stored-definition expansion publish their batch before reduce_and_solve, and generic post-operations run after publication. Ordinary source reduction itself builds a new local vector and observes the same row checks. Most post-operations reset the theory-rewriter cache before reduction; max_bv_sharing invokes ordinary reduction directly as source does. Term-ITE definitions remain appended after transformed originals before its post-reduction. NNF checks cancellation after normalization and after each introduced-definition/main-formula rewrite, before pushing that result; it publishes no partially normalized vector. Inconsistency is now the source explicit scoped flag, replacing repeated scans of the published assertion vector. In-place value propagation marks an unchanged false row as inconsistent as well as a newly false row. Public assertion error rollback and kernel close preserve/release the added state.

Persistent asserted-formula scoped substitution (2026-10-25 UTC): replaced committed-prefix reconstruction with the source lifetime-owned expression substitution and concrete scoped wrapper. MBQI pinned counterexamples and base-restart publication (2026-10-25 UTC): replaced direct counterexample queue insertion with the source model_checker new-instance owner. Capture stores concrete expression bindings and pins every binding and quantifier, without creating enodes or changing registry fingerprints/statistics. A complete owner is published only after all pins succeed; failed capture releases its constructed prefix. Duplicate candidates are retained until the source registry publication boundary. Pending instances survive decision-scope pop independently of obsolete enodes. Restart skips quantifiers removed by backtracking, reinternalizes surviving binding expressions at the captured generation, adds the source generation/min-top/max-top tuple to the registry, and releases pins after publication. Reset/close release all pending owners, including failed-restart prefixes; restart restores the native generation field on success or error.

Corrected generation provenance: unrestricted counterexamples retain max(quantifier generation, 0), rather than borrowing an existing representative's generation. Restricted finite and auxiliary counterexamples carry the generation returned by the actual model-finder inverse lookup and combine it with the quantifier generation. Existing context-recovery tests still require the oldest equality-class member to be captured, while fingerprint canonicalization remains deferred until registry insertion. A separate actual-inverse test distinguishes generation 13 from the existing binding enode generation, checking the retained generation through capture and publication.

The quantifier model-check dispatch now requests RESTART only when failed model checking actually retained new instances; pending valid instances take priority even if another quantifier exhausted checking. It no longer schedules or materializes instances at the rejected candidate's decision scope. Model-check RESTART forces a return to the current search base even when adaptive agility would normally suppress a restart. This uses the shared restart control/threshold/statistics path and stops later clause maintenance after a restart conflict. The default concrete MBQI restart runs model-finder first and model-checker second, gated by MBQI being enabled; ordinary propagation later consumes the published registry entries.

Five new regressions cover duplicate capture and binding pin lifetime across deleted decision enodes, obsolete quantifier skipping, actual inverse-generation provenance, first-success capture/restart allocation campaigns and destruction of stopped owners, and an end-to-end rejected candidate requiring forced base restart under an adaptive policy that would otherwise skip it. Default quantifier eager/lazy multipattern scheduling (2026-10-25 UTC): replaced the single-owner eager treatment of every trigger with the source default plugin's two concrete SMTMAM owners. Unary triggers are eager. Non-unary multipatterns use the live qi.max_multi_patterns limit, plus one extra eager slot when no unary trigger exists; remaining patterns belong to the lazy matcher. Ordinary propagation consumes only eager matching work. Lazy dirty state alone does not request propagation. Full final checking processes the existing delayed-instance queue, then performs the bounded lazy rematch and lets resulting context work request continuation. The optional source lazy-instantiation flag runs the same rematch in non-full preflight while preserving its DONE return boundary.

The lazy matching allowance is reset per search and each increment is individually trailed, preserving source behavior when init_search resets the current counter inside an existing user scope. Scope pop undoes actual increments instead of restoring an obsolete pre-search counter snapshot. Both matcher owners receive relevant-enode notifications and disabled-relevancy new-enode scans; only the eager owner receives equality invalidation. Source E-matching/nonempty-registry gates now apply to those event paths. Arithmetic and array sharing queries consult ground subterms from both owners. Constructor and live parameter refresh carry eager limits, lazy allowance and lazy-instantiation controls from their owning QI state; installed trigger partitions retain their source activation-time lifetime.
